Opensidian 0.9.6 is a bug-fix and feature release on top of 0.9.5. Most of the fixes make the editor, tabs, search, links and graph behave like stock Obsidian 1.13.7. The Linux downloads are the same as 0.9.5: two AppImages, Flatpak, RPM and DEB, each for Linux x86_64 and aarch64. New in this release: the first macOS builds (Apple silicon and Intel, not signed by Apple yet, see "macOS (unsigned)" below) and a CycloneDX SBOM for each platform and architecture.

Every file below has a GitHub artifact attestation (SLSA build provenance). It proves that this repository's `release.yml` workflow built the file on GitHub-hosted runners.

**SHA256SUMS is GPG-signed by the maintainer** (`SHA256SUMS.asc`, key `A6E6 9ED6 BC47 79F3 2817  2148 4CC1 AFDE 15B6 4EA3`, the same key as v0.9.5).

**The RPMs are not signed.** CI uses no RPM signing key. Check the RPMs the same way as every other file: with `SHA256SUMS` and `gh attestation verify` (see Verification).

## macOS (unsigned)

0.9.6 is the first release with macOS downloads:

- `opensidian-0.9.6-macos-aarch64-unsigned.app.zip`: Apple silicon (M1 and newer)
- `opensidian-0.9.6-macos-x86_64-unsigned.app.zip`: Intel Macs
- `opensidian-0.9.6-macos-<arch>.cdx.json` (+ `.sha256`): the macOS SBOM per architecture, scanned for CVEs in CI (fails closed)

Both builds come from native GitHub-hosted macOS runners, and the full test suite passes on each architecture before the release is assembled. **They are not signed or notarized by Apple yet.** Gatekeeper therefore blocks the first launch with a message that the app "cannot be opened" or is "from an unidentified developer". To open it:

1. Check the download first (see Verification), unzip it and move `Opensidian.app` to Applications.
2. Right-click (or Control-click) `Opensidian.app` and choose **Open**, then **Open** again in the dialog.
3. If macOS still refuses, open **System Settings › Privacy & Security**, scroll to the message about Opensidian and click **Open Anyway**.

You only need to do this once. Apple code signing and notarization are coming soon. (PR #248, PR #252)

## Features

### Mermaid, code highlighting and math
- Mermaid diagrams in notes render in reading view and Live Preview. Mermaid is vendored (12.3.0) and runs in strict mode behind the stock trust guard. `loadMermaid()` works for plugins. (#187, PR #232, PR #255)
- Fenced code blocks are syntax-highlighted with the vendored Prism, in reading view and Live Preview. (#186, PR #231)
- `$…$` and `$$…$$` math is typeset with the vendored MathJax, in reading view and Live Preview. (#185, PR #233)

### Languages (#220)
- The UI is translated into English, Simplified Chinese, Korean, Russian, Spanish and Japanese (Project Fluent). There is a new Language setting, and by default the language follows the system. (PR #228)

### Settings › Security (#144)
- A new Security section has toggles for external resources (images, audio, video) and for cutting community plugins off the network, plus a Lockdown switch. (PR #193)

## Fixes

### Editor
- Backspace moves the cursor with the text: the caret is repainted after the line re-renders. (#241, PR #247)
- Enter on a numbered task item counts up instead of repeating the number. (#154, PR #235)
- Ctrl+L on a task with a custom status (`[/]`, `[-]`, `[>]`) resets the status in place instead of adding a second checkbox. (#153, PR #234)
- Ctrl+L over several selected lines toggles every line, not just the last one. (#155, PR #223)
- Delete paragraph (Ctrl+D) on the last line no longer leaves an empty line behind. (#152, PR #227)
- Format commands from the palette (such as Toggle bold) keep the selection, so running one again unwraps. (#160, PR #216)
- Tab / Shift+Tab on a multi-line selection keeps the selection. (#161, PR #215)
- `[[` link completion typed in front of an existing link replaces the `[[` you typed, not the existing link. (#162, PR #211)
- Add tag keeps the selected text and puts `#` in front of it. (#156, PR #219)
- Find & Replace moves on to the next match when the replacement still matches the search. (#170, PR #217)
- Find in note: holding Enter (key repeat) no longer leaves the editor's focus and selection hooked for the rest of the session. (#165, PR #218)
- Live Preview: switching modes at the end of a long note no longer drifts the top line up. (#183, PR #229)
- Clicking a checklist box no longer waits for the autosave or a scan of the note. (#128, PR #134)

### Tabs, windows and sidebars
- Closing the last tab leaves an empty "New tab", as in stock Obsidian. (#242, PR #245)
- "Close all" on a single pane keeps Undo close tab working. (#175, PR #200)
- The tab menu's "Reading view" and "Source mode" entries toggle back and forth, and their rows line up as in stock Obsidian. (#179, PR #205; #214, PR #236)
- The window title shows the name of a focused graph or other view tab. (#177, PR #221)
- A collapsed left sidebar stays collapsed after a restart with every tab closed. (#158, PR #225)
- Inline title: clicking away commits the rename, as in stock Obsidian. Escape still reverts it. (#159, PR #222)
- An Excalidraw drawing can be renamed from its tab and from its view-header title. (#239, PR #243)
- Hotkeys that use the `+` key (such as Ctrl+Shift+=) survive a restart, and a Space hotkey has a label. (#163, PR #224)

### Links, search and explorer
- Ctrl+click on a wikilink, Ctrl+Enter in the quick switcher and Ctrl+click or middle-click on a search result open the new tab to the right of the active tab. (#171, PR #213; #173, PR #203)
- Search: text typed just before a flashed match is not highlighted as part of the match. (#174, PR #208)
- Backlinks / Outgoing links no longer show duplicated or stale rows after you switch notes quickly. (#176, PR #209)
- Backlinks: an Unlinked mentions row highlights its own occurrence of the note name. (#178, PR #206)
- File explorer: dragging a note onto another note's row moves it into that row's folder, not to the vault root. (#157, PR #210)
- File explorer: a plain click on a canvas file opens it in the active tab. (#169, PR #212)
- Quick switcher: Ctrl+Alt+Enter on a canvas row opens the canvas in a right split. (#168, PR #204)
- A canvas embed is resolved the same way as a canvas link. (#180, PR #207)

### Graph
- Horizontal scrolling (sideways touchpad swipe or tilt wheel) no longer zooms the graph out. (#172, PR #199)
- Opening or reopening a graph no longer leaks the previous graph through a display-resolution listener. (#166, PR #202)
- Internal: the graph test markers handle `]`, `,` and `|` in a graph search or note name. (#164, PR #201)

### Audio and plugins
- A saved recording stores its duration, so the player no longer shows a spinner. (#197, PR #226)
- Recording and media cards on a canvas play in restricted vaults too (click to play). (#196, PR #198)
- Audio recorder: while the core recorder holds the microphone, no plugin can get a microphone stream. (#136, PR #230)
- Very deep folder trees (hundreds of nested folders) no longer crash the app while the vault is scanned: the vault, canvas and index walks are iterative and depth-bounded instead of recursive. This crash first showed on macOS. (PR #257)
- Plugins get a page-global `process` with stock stdio, so plugins such as Copilot start again (they failed on `process.stdout.isTTY`). (#253, PR #254)

### Supply chain, packaging and build
- Every dependency is pinned to a version and a hash (the scanners are the exception), and CI enforces this with `pin-check`. This covers the AppImage apt set, the Flatpak runtime, the toolchain and the CodeMirror inputs. (#189, PR #237)
- Each release now ships a CycloneDX SBOM per architecture (`opensidian-0.9.6-<arch>.cdx.json` + `.sha256`). The SBOM is built inside the pinned AppImage container and CI scans it for CVEs, failing closed. (#188, PR #190, PR #249)
- The AppImage build moved to a current Ubuntu snapshot (snapshot.ubuntu.com 20261119T120000Z, previously 20261004T000000Z). The bundle's CVEs that have a fixed Ubuntu version went from 45 to 0, and the scanners run their newest pinned versions.
- Mermaid 11.17.2 → 12.3.0: this fixes the bundled KaTeX advisory GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7, plus DOMPurify and js-yaml. (PR #255)
- The Fluent license file is locked by a commit-pinned source URL and sha256. (PR #244)
- The Flatpak metadata lists the 0.9.6 release.

## Known issues
- cargo vet: two transitive crates are **exempted** instead of audited: `self_cell` 1.3.0 and `type-map` 0.5.1. Both come in through Mozilla's Fluent (`fluent-bundle`, `intl-memoizer`) for the UI translations. No trusted published audit covers them, and no newer version exists. The exemptions are temporary, and we will revisit them by 2027-02-19. (PR #256)
- The AppImages, DEB and RPM need glibc 2.43 or newer (they are built on Ubuntu 26), so they do not start on older distros such as Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or Debian 12. Opensidian supports current distros only. On an older distro, use the Flatpak, which brings its own runtime.

## Verification
Download every file of this release into one directory, then:

```sh
# 1. checksums: every file must report OK
#    (on macOS: shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS)
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS

# 2. build provenance: each file was built by this repository's
#    release workflow on GitHub Actions
for f in opensidian-0.9.6-x86_64* opensidian-0.9.6-aarch64* opensidian-0.9.6-macos-* SHA256SUMS; do
  gh attestation verify "$f" -R jpzk/opensidian
done

# 3. release attestation: this release is immutable; the tag and
#    every file are pinned by a GitHub release attestation
gh release verify v0.9.6 -R jpzk/opensidian
for f in opensidian-0.9.6-x86_64* opensidian-0.9.6-aarch64* opensidian-0.9.6-macos-* SHA256SUMS SHA256SUMS.asc; do
  gh release verify-asset v0.9.6 "$f" -R jpzk/opensidian
done
```

The RPMs are unsigned, so `rpm -K` reports no signature. Use the checks above for them.

**Signature:** the maintainer signs `SHA256SUMS`. Import the key from https://github.com/jpzk.gpg and check the file with `gpg --verify SHA256SUMS.asc SHA256SUMS`. The key fingerprint is `A6E6 9ED6 BC47 79F3 2817  2148 4CC1 AFDE 15B6 4EA3`.
